Visit note | 2025-11-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Mizanur Sarkar, 46, male. Mr. Sarkar presents today explaining that he has been suffering from a poor appetite along with a fever that seems to climb slightly higher each day for over a week. He works as a nurse and notes that his symptoms began a few days after eating street food at a fair in Shyamoli. He has a known history of Hypothyroidism, for which he takes his regular treatment. He denies any severe headache, abdominal pain, or respiratory distress. On examination: temperature 101.3°F, BP 111/77 mmHg, pulse 106 bpm, weight 82 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the right lower quadrant, and chest sounds are clear. Assessment: Typhoid fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat soft home-cooked food, drink boiled or bottled water only, and strictly avoid street food. Follow-up is scheduled in 7 days with a repeat blood count.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Jesmin Patwary, 65, female. Mrs. Patwary returns for review, stating she was alerted by a high blood pressure reading on a pharmacy machine and has been experiencing persistent headaches upon waking up in the morning. She works as a madrasa teacher and mentions this reading was picked up at a pharmacy in Khulna while buying other medicines. She has no other significant chronic medical conditions and denies chest pain or shortness of breath. On examination: BP 156/98 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 89 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added murmurs, and peripheral pulses are intact. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check her blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Nargis Ahmed, 20, female. Ms. Ahmed attends for follow-up regarding her breathing, reporting ongoing coughing spells at night accompanied by noticeable wheezing. She works as a homemaker and explains that her symptoms flared during the severe winter smog in Shyamoli. She has no other chronic illnesses and denies any fever or chest discomfort. On examination: SpO2 93%, BP 134/80 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 58 kg. Chest auscultation reveals mild bilateral expiratory wheeze. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Ishrat Kabir, 73, female. Mrs. Kabir returns for review, complaining of a tingling sensation like pins and needles in her extremities, with symptoms notably worse at night. She works as a farmer and notes her discomfort has been worse since walking barefoot at home in Badda. Her medical history is significant for Hypothyroidism. She denies any muscle weakness, visual changes, or recent falls. On examination: reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 122/70 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 48 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and reflexes are sluggish. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 04:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Nupur Das, 48, female. Mrs. Das presents for her first visit complaining of a cough productive of yellow or green sputum, sharp chest pain when taking a deep breath, and a high fever. She works as a hotel receptionist and notes her illness started after a long cold boat trip near Narayanganj. She has no other chronic medical conditions and denies previous respiratory issues. On examination: temperature 102.4°F, BP 111/81 mmHg, pulse 108 bpm, SpO2 91%, weight 43 kg. Chest examination reveals bronchial breath sounds and crackles over the right lower zone. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and to return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 04:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Ehsan Bepari, 27, male. Mr. Bepari returns for follow-up regarding an itchy skin condition that became worse in humid weather; he presents with an itchy rash that got worse after using a steroid cream from a pharmacy, noting a ring-shaped itchy red rash with spreading edges. He works as a homemaker and mentions the trouble began during the humid monsoon in Badda. He has a known comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any systemic symptoms or joint pain. On examination: affected area about 9 cm across, BP 123/79 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 64 kg. The border is well-demarcated with central clearing. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep the skin dry, do not share towels, and wash clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-25 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Hafiz Mollah, 45, male. Mr. Mollah attends for a follow-up consultation regarding his ongoing worries about sleep, waking up exhausted, and experiencing trouble falling asleep most nights. He works as an NGO field officer and states his sleep disturbance began after starting rotating shifts at a factory in Farmgate. He has no other medical conditions and denies daytime hallucinations or depressive ideation. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 24, BP 116/77 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 71 kg. Patient appears fatigued but alert and oriented. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 09:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Bushra Shikder, 32, female. Ms. Shikder returns for follow-up reporting persistent acne, noticeable weight gain, and unwanted extra hair on her face. She works as a textile engineer and mentions these issues were noticed after a friend in Mirpur suggested testing; she presents with no periods for six months with no acne or weight gain in an atypical presentation. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies pelvic pain or severe headaches. On examination: BMI 33.0, BP 112/76 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 80 kg. Systemic examination is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ehsan Chowdhury, 20, male. He works as an office cleaner and explains that his discomfort began after gaining weight while working from home in Faridpur. He has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. He denies dysphagia or unintentional weight loss. On examination: BMI 26.2, BP 131/70 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 48 kg. Abdomen is soft with no epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:00 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ashraf Pramanik, 47, male. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Habib Akand, 21, male. Skin is oily with scattered papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Sohel Mondal, 21, male. Mr. Mondal returns for follow-up, reporting a complete lack of interest in his usual activities and a persistently low mood lasting for over three weeks. He works as an architect and states his symptoms began after moving away from his family to Jashore. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies psychotic symptoms. On examination: PHQ-9 score 10, BP 130/70 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 66 kg. Patient appears subdued but cooperative. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Tariq Islam, 55, male. Mr. Islam attends for follow-up reporting no physical symptoms, but notes high cholesterol on a routine test and mentions a family history where his father had a heart attack at 55. He works as a pharmacist and states the high reading was found after a relative's heart attack in Motijheel prompted testing. He has a history of Essential hypertension. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.5 mmol/L, BP 152/89 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 61 kg. Heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Jubayer Siddique, 78, male. Mr. Siddique returns for a follow-up visit, complaining of recurrent dizzy spells and an irregular fast heartbeat. He works as a tailor and states these episodes were first felt while watching television at home in Sirajganj. He has no other major chronic illnesses and denies chest pain or syncope. On examination: pulse 112 bpm and irregular, BP 116/81 mmHg, weight 82 kg. Cardiac auscultation confirms an irregularly irregular rhythm with variable pulse volume. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Hafiz Siddique, 23, male. He was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-11-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Morium Kabir, 31, female.
